name: naabu - Fast Port Scanner (ProjectDiscovery)
description: naabu is a fast SYN/CONNECT port scanner from ProjectDiscovery, built for large host lists and automation. It quickly finds open ports, integrates with the PD toolchain (subfinder -> naabu -> httpx -> nuclei), and can hand results straight to nmap for service/version detail.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  go install github.com/projectdiscovery/naabu/v2/cmd/naabu@latest    # needs libpcap for SYN

=== SCAN ===
  naabu -host <target>                    # top 100 by default
  naabu -host <target> -top-ports 1000
  naabu -host <target> -p -               # all 65535 ports
  naabu -host <target> -p 80,443,8080,8443

=== LISTS / RANGES ===
  naabu -list <file>
  naabu -host <cidr>

=== SCAN TYPE / SPEED ===
  naabu -host <target> -s s               # SYN (needs root)
  naabu -host <target> -s c               # CONNECT
  naabu -host <target> -rate 1000

=== PIPE TO NMAP FOR SERVICE DETAIL ===
  naabu -host <target> -top-ports 1000 -nmap-cli 'nmap -sV -sC'

=== CHAIN ===
  subfinder -d <domain> -silent | naabu -silent | httpx -silent

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  nmap            # richer service/script detection
  masscan         # highest raw speed
  rustscan        # fast + nmap handoff

examples.label: Hand off open ports to nmap

recommended.note: masscan for maximum raw scan speed.
rustscan is a similar fast scanner with nmap handoff.
Follow up open ports with nmap service detection.

defense.why_it_works: Port scanning probes TCP/UDP ports to find listening services. naabu optimizes for speed and volume, so it completes enumeration quickly but generates a recognizable burst of connection attempts.
defense.impact: Rapid discovery of the open-service attack surface across many hosts.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1046] High count of distinct destination ports from one source in a short window; many SYNs without completed handshakes (SYN scan); firewall/IDS scan signatures; connection attempts to closed ports.
defense.artifacts: Firewall/flow logs (many dports/one src), IDS portscan alerts, half-open SYN counts, connection-refused spikes.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=firewall action=allowed OR action=blocked
| stats dc(dest_port) as ports count by src_ip, dest_ip, bin(_time,1m)
| where ports > 100
defense.sentinel_kql:
CommonSecurityLog
| summarize Ports=dcount(DestinationPort), Count=count() by SourceIP, DestinationIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where Ports > 100
defense.prevention: Restrict exposed ports (least surface, allowlist ingress); IDS/IPS port-scan detection and rate limiting; deny-by-default firewalling; honeypots/canary ports to catch scanning; monitor for high-fanout connection sources.

detections.name: Fast multi-port scan from single source (naabu/masscan)
detections.logic:
CommonSecurityLog
| summarize Ports=dcount(DestinationPort), Count=count() by SourceIP, DestinationIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where Ports > 100
detections.tuning: Allowlist sanctioned scanners; alert on external sources
